items.title: How long do you go between washing sheets?
items.html: Doc poll: sheets and towels are supposed to be every one to two weeks. A Sleep Advisor study put the average closer to 24 days (25 for pillowcases). A UK look at single men found a majority waiting about four months. About 5 percent of people wash them once or twice a year. Phone: honest number, then whether the guest-room sheets are a different story. Keep it light.

items.html: Monday birthdays if you need a tomorrow hit: Kate Winslet 51, Jesse Eisenberg 43, Neil deGrasse Tyson 68, Brian Johnson of AC/DC 79. Soft: who you share a day with.

items.title: Texas volleyball vs Alabama, 2 p.m.
items.html: Gregory Gym, 2 p.m. If the park is a no. Soft: the indoor plan that does not involve mud. Monster Truck Wars are also at the Expo Center today if someone needs louder.

items.title: Trail of Lights tickets are already on sale
items.html: 62nd H-E-B Trail of Lights is Dec 10–23 at Zilker. Free nights Dec 10–11 and 13–17. Paid nights $8, kids under 12 free. Soft: buying December lights in October — organized, or unhinged? More here →

items.title: Longhorns are on a bye
items.html: Texas is off this weekend after the 20–17 win at Tennessee. Next is Red River: Texas vs Oklahoma, Saturday Oct 10, 2:30 p.m. CT, Cotton Bowl, ABC. Soft: what do you do with a bye Sunday if you are not at ACL?

items.title: Smiley (Indy) — The Sunday plan that is still unlocked
items.html: Where it came from: Plan-changed open. How they ran it: Host states the plan, then the thing that undid it. JB & Sandy Austin version: “We’re doing ACL Sunday.” Then the mud photos, then the couch. Who is still going, and who already changed the group chat? Audio: recommend a plan-change sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: Smiley (Indy) — The thing you packed and will not use
items.html: Where it came from: Just-in-case bit. How they ran it: Host names the item that never left the bag. JB & Sandy Austin version: Poncho, backup socks, the printed schedule. What did you bring to Zilker that is still in the car? Audio: recommend a packing sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: Daly Migs (Seattle) — Low-tech wins the park
items.html: Where it came from: Old-school vs. app. How they ran it: Host pits the paper against the phone. JB & Sandy Austin version: The ACL app dies and the friend with the printed schedule becomes the leader. Who still trusts a paper map? Audio: recommend a wrong-turn sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: Daly Migs (Seattle) — Pretend the shoes are fine
items.html: Where it came from: Pretend-not-notice. How they ran it: Host names the thing everyone can see and nobody mentions. JB & Sandy Austin version: “These are waterproof.” They were not. How long do you pretend before the weekend is over? Audio: recommend a squish sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: Valentine — The compliment that was actually a warning
items.html: Where it came from: Kindness phone. How they ran it: Host reads a nice line that meant the opposite. JB & Sandy Austin version: “You look ready for the park.” Translation: those shoes will not survive. What compliment was a warning? Audio: recommend a too-sweet sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: On Air with Ryan Seacrest — Tiny win, then the song
items.html: Where it came from: Small-win closer. How they ran it: One real win, then a song that matches the mood. JB & Sandy Austin version: Found a dry patch of grass. Made it to noon volleyball instead of the mud. What is the tiny Sunday win? Audio: recommend a tiny-win sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: Miguel & Holly (Tampa Mix) — The meal that got ruined
items.html: Where it came from: Food-order phone. How they ran it: Host names the order, then the thing that wrecked it. JB & Sandy Austin version: Breakfast taco in the car, then the group chat says “we’re going.” Who ate the festival meal in the driveway? Audio: recommend a food sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: Dwyer & Michaels — The house rule that failed
items.html: Where it came from: House-rule bit. How they ran it: Host states the rule, then the Sunday that broke it. JB & Sandy Austin version: “One festival day.” It became two, and the laundry is still in the basket. What house rule did the weekend kill? Audio: recommend a rule-break sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: Heidi & Frank (KLOS) — One more time
items.html: Where it came from: One-more-time phone. How they ran it: Host asks who is going back for the closer. JB & Sandy Austin version: Twenty One Pilots or The xx at 8:30. Who is actually going back, and who is watching the 3:35 stream in socks? Audio: recommend a one-more-set sting; otherwise pure talk.

items.title: Closer — Most Austin thing
items.html: Where it came from: City-pitch closer. How they ran it: Host takes the most Austin detail of the day. JB & Sandy Austin version: Skipping the headline clash to sit in Gregory Gym at noon, then arguing about sheet-washing on the way home. What is the most Austin thing you did this weekend? Audio: recommend a city sting; otherwise pure talk.
